title: Frontend: Product Cart with Discounts
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Product Cart with Discounts. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Export App({products=[{id:a,name:Alpha,price:100},{id:b,name:Beta,price:250}]}). Add[data-add=ID] and Remove[data-remove=ID] change integer quantities, clamped to zero. Render quantity[data-quantity=ID]. Discount select is 0/10 percent; output[data-testid=total] is subtotal minus once-rounded percentage discount in cents. Render all products. Product prices are valid integer cents; this local pricing preview is not authoritative checkout.
constraints: Export default App. Only react and react/jsx-runtime imports are supported. The DOM contract and supplied props define the exercise.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Normalize products and cart quantities by ID.
alternativeApproaches: Design a server quote/version mechanism so payment uses the exact accepted pricing snapshot.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Expired coupon; stacked discounts; quantity changes.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
